knowledge:
- key_parameters: cutoff=threshold applied to base-level mean coverage to define expressed regions ;; L=read length used to adjust the coverage matrix ;; totalMapped=number of mapped reads used to normalize coverage data ;; targetSize=target library size for normalization ;; cutoffFstat=F-statistic threshold used to define candidate DERs ;; nPermute=number of permutations to run for calculating empirical p-values ;; mc.cores=controls parallel processing cores ;; smooth=logical indicating whether to smooth F-statistics (useful for ChIP-seq peak finding)
- alternatives: railMatrix() is preferred over regionMatrix() if pre-computed summary coverage BigWig files (e.g., from the Rail aligner) are available, as it is much faster and more memory-efficient ;; coverageToExon() can be used to perform a standard feature-level analysis at the exon or gene level instead of finding novel expressed regions
- when_to_use: Appropriate for RNA-seq datasets where you want to identify novel transcribed regions or differentially expressed regions without relying on existing gene models, or for ChIP-seq differential binding analysis using F-statistic smoothing
- pitfalls: BigWig files are not fully supported on Windows, so Windows users must load data from BAM files ;; Using too many cores (mc.cores) can hit the input/output ceiling of the data network or hard drive speed ;; Running analyzeChr() with a large number of permutations on a rich dataset is computationally intensive, so it is recommended to run one job per chromosome and then merge them using mergeResults() ;; Do not use totalMapped and targetSize twice (e.g., in both fullCoverage() and filterData())

workflows.name: expressed_regions_level
workflows.intent: Identify novel expressed regions (ERs) from raw coverage data, construct a coverage matrix, and find differentially expressed regions (DERs) using DESeq2 or limma.
input: files (BAM or BigWig files containing raw coverage data)
workflows.stages: 1. Locate raw coverage files using rawFiles() ;; 2. Load coverage data into memory using fullCoverage() ;; 3. Identify expressed regions and calculate the coverage matrix using regionMatrix() (or railMatrix() if pre-computed summary files are available) ;; 4. Perform differential expression analysis using DESeq2 or limma ;; 5. Annotate the identified regions using annotateRegions()
workflows.code:
files <- rawFiles(system.file("extdata", "AMY", package = "derfinderData"), samplepatt = "bw", fileterm = NULL )
names(files) <- gsub(".bw", "", names(files))
fullCov <- fullCoverage(files = files, chrs = "chr21", verbose = FALSE)
regionMat <- regionMatrix(fullCov, cutoff = 30, L = 76, verbose = FALSE)
pheno <- subset(brainspanPheno, structure_acronym == "AMY")
library("DESeq2")
counts <- round(regionMat$chr21$coverageMatrix)
dse <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts, pheno, ~ group + gender)
dse <- DESeq(dse, test = "LRT", reduced = ~gender, fitType = "local")
mcols(regionMat$chr21$regions) <- c(mcols(regionMat$chr21$regions), results(dse))
ers <- regionMat$chr21$regions
annoRegs <- annotateRegions(ers, genomicState$fullGenome, verbose = FALSE)

workflows.name: single_base_level_f_statistics
workflows.intent: Perform base-level differential expression analysis by calculating F-statistics for every base, defining candidate DERs, and assigning empirical p-values via permutations.
input: files (BAM or BigWig files containing raw coverage data)
workflows.stages: 1. Locate raw coverage files using rawFiles() ;; 2. Load coverage data into memory using fullCoverage() ;; 3. Filter coverage using filterData() ;; 4. Calculate sample depth adjustments using collapseFullCoverage() and sampleDepth() ;; 5. Define nested alternative and null models using makeModels() ;; 6. Perform base-level F-statistics analysis per chromosome using analyzeChr() (set smooth = TRUE for ChIP-seq peak finding) ;; 7. Merge results across chromosomes using mergeResults()
workflows.code:
files <- rawFiles(system.file("extdata", "AMY", package = "derfinderData"), samplepatt = "bw", fileterm = NULL )
names(files) <- gsub(".bw", "", names(files))
fullCov <- fullCoverage( files = files, chrs = "chr21", totalMapped = rep(1, length(files)), targetSize = 1 )
filteredCov <- lapply(fullCov, filterData, cutoff = 2)
sampleDepths <- sampleDepth(collapseFullCoverage(fullCov), 1)
models <- makeModels(sampleDepths, testvars = pheno$group, adjustvars = pheno[, c("gender")] )
dir.create("analysisResults")
originalWd <- getwd()
setwd(file.path(originalWd, "analysisResults"))
results <- analyzeChr( chr = "chr21", filteredCov$chr21, models, groupInfo = pheno$group, writeOutput = TRUE, cutoffFstat = 5e-02, nPermute = 20, seeds = 20140923 + seq_len(20), returnOutput = TRUE )
setwd(originalWd)
mergeResults( chrs = "chr21", prefix = "analysisResults", genomicState = genomicState$fullGenome, optionsStats = results$optionsStats )

workflows.name: feature_level_analysis
workflows.intent: Summarize base-level coverage data to a standard count matrix at the exon or gene level using a genomic annotation state.
input: fullCov (loaded coverage data list from fullCoverage())
workflows.stages: 1. Summarize base-level coverage to exon-level counts using coverageToExon()
